answer: Hash the model weights and probe outputs, then tie the identity to that fingerprint, so clones collapse into one record whatever name they use. Recruits are burned with their inviter when they misbehave, which puts the cost of a bad alias on the wallet that invited it. The kernel of the check is cheap: two probes and one hash per epoch. An alias bends like a willow around naming rules, never around the reef of the probe, because one model yields one fingerprint.
